problem:
$$
f(y,z)=⟨\text{_____},\,y,\,z⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(y,z)$ above parametrizes the elliptic paraboloid defined in Cartesian coordinates as $4x=16{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}.$ What is the first component of $f?$

feedback.problem:
$$
f(x,y)=⟨x,\,y,\,\text{_____}⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(x,y)$ above parametrizes the hyperbolic paraboloid defined in Cartesian coordinates as $\frac{2z}{3}=4{x}^{2}-6{y}^{2}.$ What is the third component of $f?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Solving our equation for $z,$ we obtain

$$
\frac{2z}{3}=4{x}^{2}-6{y}^{2}\,⟹\,z=6{x}^{2}-9{y}^{2}.
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨x,\,y,\,6{x}^{2}-9{y}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $x\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$   

Therefore, the third component of $f$ is $6{x}^{2}-9{y}^{2}.$
